answer_1.quote: In recent years, sequence-to-sequence neural models have enabled great progress in abstractive summarization.

answer_2.quote: We use ROUGE, in its commonly used three flavours of ROUGE-1 (noted R-1), ROUGE-2 (noted R-2) and ROUGE-L (noted R-L) for summarization evaluation. We also leverage recently introduced model based evaluation methods BERTScore (noted BS) and BARTScore (noted BaS).

answer_4.quote: We asked three different humans to evaluate 50 randomly sampled test summaries for each dataset. Human raters were graduate students with professional English proficiency (TOEFL scores above 100 out of 120).
answer_4.guideline: Humans were shown the source document alongside the top beam search summary from PEGASUS, and the corresponding summary candidate selected by SummaReranker. They were asked to choose which one they believe is more faithful.
